questions.q: Which state of matter has particles that are packed closely in a fixed pattern?
questions.explain: In a solid the particles are packed tightly in a regular pattern and can only vibrate in place.

questions.q: A balloon left in a hot car gets bigger. What is the best explanation?
options: The gas particles move faster and spread further apart
questions.explain: Heating gives the particles more kinetic energy, so they move faster and push further apart. The particles themselves do not grow.

sections.title: True or false
sections.intro: Decide whether each statement is true or false.

questions.q: Particles in a gas are far apart and move freely in all directions.
questions.explain: Gas particles have the most energy of the three states and spread out to fill their container.

questions.q: Melting changes a liquid into a solid.
questions.explain: Melting changes a solid into a liquid. A liquid changing into a solid is freezing.

questions.q: Match each change of state in column A with its description in column B.
questions.explain: Evaporation and condensation are opposites, as are melting and freezing.

questions.q: Find the matching pairs: link each word to its meaning.
pairs: Particles spreading from high to low concentration
Particles moving further apart when heated
Particles moving closer together when cooled

questions.scenario: Thandi puts a drop of food colouring into a glass of hot water and another drop into a glass of cold water. After two minutes the colour has spread through the hot water, but not yet through the cold water.

questions.q: What process spreads the colour through the water?
questions.explain: The colouring particles move from where they are concentrated to where there are fewer of them: diffusion.

questions.q: Put the steps of Thandi's investigation in the correct order.
steps: Pour equal amounts of hot and cold water into two glasses
Add one drop of food colouring to each glass
Compare how far the colour has spread
questions.explain: Set up a fair test first, then add the colouring at the same time, wait, and only then compare.

questions.q: The colour spreads faster in hot water because its particles move faster.
questions.explain: Higher temperature means more kinetic energy, so diffusion happens faster.
